key_insight: A stacking machine-learning model using pre-operative clinical features accurately predicted Mohs cases likely to need 13 or more sections.
clinical_relevance: If validated externally, this could help schedule operating time, plan resources, and counsel patients before Mohs micrographic surgery.
method: 408 consecutive Mohs procedures were analyzed with 16 pre-operative clinical variables.
Thirty machine-learning models were compared, including ensemble, boosting, neural network, SVM, and traditional classifiers.
Performance used 5-fold stratified cross-validation plus an independent test set, with SHAP for feature importance.
evidence_signal: The best model achieved a cross-validation AUC of 0.891 and a test AUC of 0.884, with tumor area the strongest predictor.
watch_item: This single-cohort model needs external validation across centers and practice patterns before routine use.
paper_title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting 13 or More Sections in Mohs Micrographic Surgery
